title: Polynomial-time certificate compilation
statement: Let $L$ and $V$ be languages of finite bit strings, and let $C,c$ be natural numbers. Suppose that for every bit string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the existence of a bit string $u$ with $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$ and the concatenation of $x$ and $u$ belonging to $V$. Suppose also that a finite deterministic machine $M$ decides $V$ in time $A(m+1)^d$ for all input lengths $m$, for natural numbers $A,d$. Then there exist natural numbers $K,r$ and a finite nondeterministic machine $N$ that decides $L$ in time $K(n+C(n+1)^c+1)^r$ for all input lengths $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $L,V$ are languages of finite bit strings
for every $x$, membership in $L$ is equivalent to a certificate $u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^c$ with $xu\in V$
$M$ is a finite deterministic machine over bits
replaced: Let $L$ be a language over the binary alphabet such that $x \in L$ exactly when some binary string $u$ with $|u| = C\,(|x|+1)^c$ has $x\,u \in V$, and let $M$ be a deterministic machine deciding the verifier language $V$ within time $A(m+1)^d$. Then there are constants $K, r$ and a nondeterministic machine deciding $L$ within time $K\,(n + C(n+1)^c + 1)^r$.
